newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts off on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts off on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Thursday in a sluggish session, with mild weather forecasts still pressuring the front of the complex though prices remained in recent technical ranges, sources said.
April slipped 3.6 cents to close at $1.838 per million British thermal units. May settled 2.9 cent lower at $1.879, Others ended mixed, with some 1998s steady to up.

"I don't see us going much lower. We're probably a dime from the bottom, but I can't imagine what's going to take us higher," said one New York-based trader, adding injection demand and cooling loads were needed to balance the market.

With more mild weather ahead, most expected cash and paper to stay on the defensive when March flows begin, with some expecting longer-term pressure, perhaps into April, until the eastern storage surplus is trimmed.
Wednesday's AGA data showed eastern inventories were 225 bcf, or 56 percent, over last year.

Technical traders still saw support in April at $1.80, then in the mid-$1.70s and the contract low of $1.701. Resistance was pegged along the down trendline in the $1.90 area, then at $1.935 and $2.04.

In the March cash, Gulf Coast prices notionally were talked little changed in the mid-to-high $1.70s. March Midcon gas also notionally held steady in the low-to-mid $1.60s. New York city gate gas for March remained at about $2.15.
The 12-month strip fell 2.1 cents to $2.019. NYMEX said an estimated 23,249 Hub contracts traded, up from Wednesday's revised tally of 21,089.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Thursday.

On the KCBT, April finished two cents lower at $1.61, while deferreds ended down by two to three cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.6 cents to 22.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 86 lots changed hands, down from Thursday's total of 167.
